items.title: There's nothing I can do*
items.content:
TL;DR: it seems to me that I am unable to do anything useful on the AI issue other than being informed. I feel bad about it.

Naive extrapolations point to extreme superintelligence in a year; I'll be 23 at that point. I keep reading about Really Trying and Getting Involved so that we hopefully don't die.

It is unclear to me that there's anything at all I can do in that regard.

Why I believe that:

- I am a 22yo undergraduate student at the only AI undergrad program in my country (Italy). I am not particularly technically or academically skilled, with Cs on average. I pass the class and move on.
- I have no money, as in, zero income at all; I can't move to London or the U.S.
- My country as a whole is not particularly influential or informed on the topic, and there is essentially no community around this. I may very realistically be one of 100-1,000 people in Italy who knows about the intellectual, forecasting and existential side of AI.
- Even the people at my own university (the literal only undergrads in Italy on AI) are stuck at GPT-4o levels. Anecdotally, they are not aware that AI can code at a professional level.

Here is what I am doing:

- I stay informed as much as possible. I regularly read LessWrong, Zvi, METR, Yudkowsky/Soares/CSET/others, as well as the various forecasts and proposals (AI 2027, AI 2040 and so on). Anything that seems useful to understand.
- I chat with people (as in, family and few friends/acquaintances) about AI, but it's not like they have much interest, and after a few minutes you've got to change the subject anyways.

That's it. I don't what else to do. Any way I spin it in my head, it appears to me that I am powerless to take any action.

I don't even want to work in AI. I already have career plans and goals in life, all of which are unrelated to AI. This post has been mostly hopeless, but I only feel that way about the current AI existential situation; things are otherwise going well....

items.title: We want to run AI safety events for you!
items.content:
TL;DR: We’re four undergraduate organizers who want to build an Events-as-a-Service (EaaS) organization to execute events for operations-constrained AI safety orgs. You cover an event’s operational costs and programming, and we'll plan and run it. Scope and timeline are negotiable. If you have an event you’d want us to help run in the next ~3 months, please fill out the form linked here! 

Background

Ops capacity is limited in the AI safety community, and events eat up a lot of it. An EaaS organization could rapidly supply ops capacity to organizations to capitalize on short convening windows, preserve capacity, and test low-hanging event ideas that otherwise would be missed.

Work with us!

We are interested in executing events-shaped projects with partner organizations in the next months for free while we build a track record. Some example events that we could help run include retreats, convenings, workshops, hackathons, socials and happy hours. We could handle lodging, travel, comms, venue, catering, and more, but the precise specifications are up for negotiation. 

Our team

We’re four undergraduate organizers with both event-ops experience and AI safety context. 

Between us, we have:

- Run a 50 person, weekend EA retreat (Fall ‘26 Northeast EA Retreat)
- Founded the UCSD and Vanderbilt AI safety groups, running multiple fellowship cohorts
- Help run a 126-member EA Intro Fellowship (Yale)
- Help run a startup accelerator, directly assisting 2 teams getting into YC

We’d be happy to provide more information on our past work and connect you with previous funders of ours if necessary. 

Depending on our growth, we may found a long-term organization and scale up capacity, or pivot to something else. We are not sure yet how many event projects we intend on taking on over the next few months. 

Contact us!

Again, please fill out this form if you are interested! We will aim to respond to all inquiries within 3 days.

items.title: I find myself confused about empathy
items.content:
Inspired by https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/xPrL2xF9iYWpPmu6B/my-empathy-is-rarely-kind

I find myself confused about empathy. I wrote this to try and deconfuse myself.

Let's take the example case of "posting bad political takes on the internet." When I see someone doing this, it bothers me. But then I remind myself of times that I've posted stuff that I later thought was bad. This establishes a certain baseline of empathy. But then I hit a problem: when I think back on those times, I feel shame. So though I get it, it basically justifies me feeling negative things towards them. If I feel negative towards myself for those things, it seems fair for me to send that their way.

But this isn't really fair, right? I'm judging them by my own values, not theirs. There are things I've said online that I do stand behind. Presumably they feel that way about this thing, even if I think it's stupid. And in fact if I follow this logic, I can build out a richer predictive model of their behavior. 

Is this the more empathetic approach? Kind of, but sometimes it leaves my actual feelings more negative than before. When I see the world through their eyes in a predictively sophisticated way, I might not like what I see. Sometimes I do find this sort of approach gives me a newfound respect for a person, but it's not guaranteed. I guess on some level it depends on… how objectively admirable the person is? Surely not, it has to be some sort of higher level intuitive moral function I find harder to shake off. But just as a practical matter, it isn't always the case that improving my predictive model for a person's behavior makes me more interpersonally sympathetic....

items.title: I'm leaving my PhD to pursue AI Safety work
items.content:
Yesterday, I told my advisors that I would be dropping out of my PhD program at the University of Michigan's School of Information. I was nervous about how to break the news to them. There was already some tension in our weekly meetings: I often voiced my dissatisfaction with the pace of academia, my interests had been drifting away from theirs, and, most of all, we disagreed on the severity of the risks AI posed.

When I walked into the room, they told me something I would have loved to hear months earlier:

“We think it’s time to get you started on some research.”

All I could say was, “I think it’s a little too late for that.”

For months, I had been proposing projects that bridged my interests with theirs, such as running studies that treated humans and LLMs as equal subjects, but they were usually turned down for not being “exciting enough”. My advisors wanted me to start with small, unpublished surveys that would "help me ask the right questions" and “develop research taste” in Human-Computer Interaction before I could propose a full study. I understood why they wanted me to gain experience first, but I felt held back after every meeting, and grew restless alongside my ambition and sense of urgency.

“I’ve been doing machine learning research independently,” I told them.

“I discovered some really interesting stuff about how to interpret neurons inside of LLMs. It’s garnered some attention, and some people are even open to funding my work. I’ll be withdrawing and moving to San Francisco at the end of the semester.”

“I had a feeling,” one of them said. “I had the opportunity to work in industry when I was in your shoes. It’s an exciting time to be in the Bay.”...

items.title: Three Things at Thirty (for dudes)
items.content:
There’s two things I really wish I’d done much earlier in life, which I cannot catch-up with, due to the realities of aging. Also one thing I did do, which I’m happy about. So if you’re near 30, here’s three things you really should do ASAP.

## 1. Test Your T

As you age and your metabolism accrues errors, your hormone levels will degrade. Testosterone is the chemical of desire. As you lose it you’ll lose your motivation to do things in general, and attendant energy levels as well. Honestly, maybe this is a good thing? Maybe as we age we should set our sights lower and accept that we’ve won our biggest victories and cultivate the fruits of our prior accomplishments rather than striving for ever greater heights.

But maybe not. Maybe it’s good to stay hungry. The good news is that testosterone is super cheap to manufacture and very easy to supplement, so you can keep it at your healthy youthful levels indefinitely. The bad news is that by the time you realize you need it, you don’t know what those levels were.

Male testosterone ranges from 300 to 1,000 ng/dL (nanograms per deciliter). This is a very wide range! You probably want to aim to restore the level your healthy young body naturally produces and has adjusted to. But if you go in and test at 300 ng/dL there is no way for your doctor to know if your base level 10 years ago was 450 or 700 or 950. He’ll probably aim for a middle line, but that’s probably an under- or overshoot.

You can’t get this information from the past once it is the past. When you want it is when you can’t get it. Head this off. Go in and get your testosterone levels tested when you’re young so that when you get older you’ll know what to restore to.

Honestly you may want to do this in your late 20s. 30 is an easy-to-remember milestone though.

items.title: Order of Operations for the Order of the Phoenix at the Hinge of History (OOO-OOP-HOH)
items.content:
Phoenix in my room at the time of writing

Phoenixes have always been my spirit animal, and I bought this tapestry long before reading Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality, however, yes, this is also the group house in which HPMOR was completed, Godric’s Hollow, which if I’m not mistaken does give us the non-exclusive, non-copyrighted, non-commercial, completely unrelated to J. K. Rowling rights to use the term “Order of the Phoenix”

Originally written November, 2025. I still endorse maybe 50-70% of this memo[1].

# 0. Preamble

With this memo, on the top floor of the tallest tower of Godric's Hollow, I instantiate the real-life Order of the Phoenix, and begin the proceedings with our group cheer which carries the initials of this memo and is hereby imbued with the full force of our collective energy-wisdom-intentionality:

# OOO-OOP-HOH!!!

Now that that’s out of the way… 

This memo began as a response to an email from Dony which I found deeply energizing and epic. In the spirit of "Yes-And," I am responding in kind. I grouped together all Dony’s ideas that seemed similar, noticed they fell into a few main categories, and prioritized them in what I believe is very roughly the order of operations in which they should be enacted. I'll start each section with some of Dony's text and then add my commentary.

1. Prioritization: Comprehensively list best project ideas and carefully pick the #1 hinge-iest project for preventing x-risk, then take the #1 hinge-iest action on it every day

2. Feedback: Publish #1 hinge-iest idea OR ship #1 hinge-iest project feature every day to real people and source high-quality feedback

I made a site that collects videos linked in LW posts and comments: https://lesstube.vercel.app/

It has over 13,000 videos collected from 19 years of LW, with frequently linked ones ranked higher. You can search by topic, browse playlists, and see the original discussions behind each video.

Inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s HackerTube: https://hackertube.org/about

It certainly "feels" viscerally healthier for my brain. I personally have this and hackertube both bookmarked on my phone and alternate between them for bedtime watching if I can't be bothered to read.

Enjoy!

items.title: Assaulted
items.content:
Walking home late at night, ahead of me under the dim glow of a street light, I saw a man coming towards me.

As he trudged forward, he spotted a jacket on the ground. People frequently scavenge around this part of town, so it wasn’t odd when he bent down, picked it up, and kept slogging along with his head hung low. Coming closer to me, I realized the sheer size of this man. He was at least a foot taller than me, and 100lbs heavier. 

When he was no more than four feet in front of me, he jerked his arms up, holding up the jacket, and politely asked, “Is this your size?” 

Confused, I replied, “No, it’s not.” 

A switch flipped in him.

He screamed, “IS THIS YOUR SIZE?!?” 

He dropped the jacket and brought up his fists, his eyes pulsing with the unmistakable look of bloodlust. Within the span of two seconds, I checked the road, saw it was empty, and sprinted across while he screamed, “YOU SHOULDN’T BE HERE.” 

On the other side, I whipped my head around. He was still just standing on his side of the street. Without thinking I shouted, “Fuck you, man! Get out of here! Go home!”

We stared each other down. Eventually, he turned away and moseyed along. I continued walking home, anxiously checking behind me every few seconds. After a few minutes, my adrenaline stopped pumping, and I began to process what had just happened. Two thoughts emerged.

The first thought was about self-preservation. Had that hulk of a man not revealed his craziness and just kept walking until he was right next to me, he could have easily body-slammed me into the iron bars of the fence next to the sidewalk, knocked me off my feet, and then pummeled me to death. I’m strong, but there’s a reason weight classes exist in fighting sports. Upon thinking this, I suddenly empathized with the quiet and restrained terror women are forced to stomach as they stay vigilant of strangers who may suddenly inflict violence upon them....

items.title: You Can Get Over Your Three-Letter Disorder
items.content:
[This post is the first post of my thirty-day writing project, where I write one blog post per day for thirty days straight. Tune in for more!]

I, for most of my life, could have been easily identified as someone with strong ADHD, OCD, and anxiety symptoms. Now I don’t really have these symptoms. What changed, and why do I think most people can do something like this?

Disclaimer: this is an opinion post done by someone without a shred of laboratory evidence for their thesis. Take it as such. I’m going to use words in this post like “definitely” and “totally possible”—this reflects what I really think (i.e., what I’d bet money on), and it’s supported by my personal experience. The plural of personal anecdote is empirical, right? Anyway.... If you disagree with me, then fine. I don’t care. You’re right. You win. I don’t know you. I’m unaware that you’re actually the one person this advice doesn’t apply to. Awesome. You can’t get over it. You’re doomed forever. Stop reading now and save your time.

## Introduction

The short answer on what changed from my childhood: I systematically changed my behavior to not exhibit any more symptoms of these disorders. To show you that this answer isn’t as trite as it seems, I’d like to take a step back and show you how I think about “three-letter disorders” (OCD, ADD, ADHD, GAD, MDD, etc.) in general. I think this is most easily introduced via an example.

Let’s say there is a kid named Johnny in your class in school, and Johnny is hyperactive, impulsive, forgetful, and a procrastinator. You end up getting tired of being around Johnny and his loser self, and so you ask him:

“Johnny, why are you so damn lazy? You are forgetful, impulsive, a procrastinator, and you distract everyone around you too! What the hell is wrong with you?”

Johnny replies,

items.title: Stroh Violin Shoulder Rest
items.content:
My
Stroh violin doesn't have a body,
which means you can't mount a regular shoulder rest.  It just has a
bit of metal:

Playing it this way is uncomfortable, and ages ago I made something
out of wood and an old 1/2 size shoulder rest I found lying around.
Then I took it
off, and it's been back to being uncomfortable.  Today I made a
new one:

It's a piece of 1/4" plywood for a full-size shoulder rest to grip, a
piece of 3/4" plywood for getting the distance right and something for
screws to bite, and then it attaches to the metal plate on the Stroh
with screws around the perimeter.

Here's me playing Sandy Boys, with intonation that's very nearly right:

youtube

It doesn't sound great, but at least it's comfortable.
